title: Methods, Classes, and Encapsulation
summary: Create focused methods and small classes with parameters, return values, constructors, private fields, validation, and clear responsibilities.

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Methods package behavior behind typed parameters and a return type. `void` means no result is returned. Java passes arguments by value; for object references, the copied reference still points to the same mutable object. A class combines state and behavior. Keep fields private, validate constructor and method inputs, and expose operations that preserve invariants rather than public mutable fields. `static` members belong to the class; instance members require an object. Use exceptions such as `IllegalArgumentException` when a caller violates a documented precondition.
keyPoints: Methods package behavior behind typed parameters and a return type.
commonMistakes: missing progress can produce an infinite loop
a void method cannot provide a result expression
